HB 2091.summary: Extends the duty to give unions employee contact information to state agencies and certain other state employers, with a temporary liability exemption tied to the state's HR technology upgrade.

tags.evidence: The requirement for public employers to provide the exclusive bargaining representative with employee contact information is extended to include the employers covered by the Personnel System Reform Act

HB 2092.summary: Creates a passenger rail advisory committee; the summary states no funding, powers, or changes to existing rules.

tags.evidence: Establishing a passenger rail advisory committee.

HB 2093.summary: Reinstates tax exemptions for the sale of precious metals and bullion.

tags.evidence: Reinstating the tax exemptions for the sale of precious metals and bullion.

HB 2094.summary: Requires county legislative authorities to appoint coroners, except large counties with medical examiners, and repeals the coroner bond requirement.

tags.evidence: Each noncharter county legislative authority must appoint a coroner, unless the county has a population of at least 250,000 and has appointed a medical examiner.

HB 2095.summary: Presumes drivers negligent in suits where vulnerable road users are hurt in crosswalks or bike lanes, adds statutory and punitive damages, and requires related training.

tags.evidence: Any driver who operates a vehicle in a manner that proximately causes the injury or death of a vulnerable user of a public way is presumed to have acted negligently
educational classes and materials regarding the offense of negligent driving with a vulnerable user victim

HB 2096.summary: Authorizes the Department of Licensing to issue confidential driver's licenses and identicards to Attorney General Office investigators for undercover work.

tags.evidence: Authorizes the DOL to issue confidential drivers' licenses and identicards to investigators employed by the AGO.

HB 2097.summary: Authorizes counties to impose a business and occupation (B&O) tax.

HB 2098.summary: Cuts public college tuition for resident undergraduates 10% yearly through 2029-30, caps later increases to wage growth, and expands state need grant eligibility.

tags.evidence: tuition operating fees for resident undergraduates at public institutions of higher education are reduced by 10 percent each academic year through the 2029-30 academic year

HB 2099.summary: Expands eligibility for the Early Childhood Education and Assistance Program (ECEAP) to include military families.

tags.evidence: Expanding access to the early childhood education and assistance program for military families.

HB 2100.summary: Creates a 5% payroll expense tax on large employers' wages above the Social Security cap, with 51% of revenue going to a new Well Washington Fund.

tags.evidence: 51 percent of revenues from the payroll expense tax will be deposited into the WWFA.
Moneys may only be spent after appropriation and may only be used for higher education programs, health care, cash assistance programs, and energy and housing programs.
